summary: Hocking State Forest tower built in 1934 as an 80-foot Aermotor design; restored by the Ohio Division of Forestry, not staffed, stairs open to climbers at their own risk when weather allows.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab

access.note: stairs open when weather allows, at climbers' own risk; a visitor account says the cab cannot be reached

visit.trail_note: parking north of the tower at OH-374 and Chapel Ridge Road; about 550 feet south on the Grandma Gatewood Trail

notes_for_editor: The ohiodnr.gov pages for this tower returned HTTP 404 when fetched, so the state's own page is unverified. The register and both guides agree on 1934 and 80 feet. The restoration has no date. The cab-access point comes from a visitor comment on the register page, not from the owner. No staffing history or notable fire was found. The record's agency (Ohio Department of Natural Resources) is unchanged; the register names the Ohio Division of Forestry as cooperator.
